subject: Commercial proposal: NovaCare RFI — surge credit float pool & true-up mechanics

Subject: Commercial proposal: NovaCare RFI — surge credit float pool & true-up mechanics

Hi Lina —

Thanks for the detailed RFI. Attached is our commercial summary (v3) that focuses on how we handle bursty traffic and true-up reconciliation for annual commitments. Key points at a glance: 

- Commit structure: monthly-banded annual commit (tokens/month floor, with optional smoothing bucket).
- Surge/floating pool: pre-funded credit pool that absorbs transient spikes; applied before overage pricing.
- True-up cadence: quarterly invoice true-up with automatic crediting for under-utilization.
- Worked example attached (see pricing_worked_example.xlsx) that shows a 3x burst event and net invoice impact.

Attachments: redwood_novacare_commercial_summary_v3.pdf (pdf)

Questions for you before we finalize for procurement:
1) Do you prefer a single annual commit or quarterly-committed tranches (we included both options in the doc)?
2) Is NovaCare open to a prepay float pool sized to 10–20% of average monthly usage, refundable at contract end?

If helpful we can convert the worked example into a short table in the SOW/Term Sheet for your procurement team.

Cheers,

Olga Petrov

Lina / Olga —

Thanks, Olga — good first pass. A couple of commercial asks from my side before we hand this to procurement: 

- Can we cap overage unit price at 1.5x list for the first 90 days after an unexpected spike if the customer engages our support team? This reduces bill-shock risk.
- Add an explicit rolling 90-day lookback for the float pool drawdown so short-term regressions restore the pool gradually rather than immediate replenishment.
- Clarify tax and region-specific billing (we should call out US sales tax vs VAT in EU if this ever scales).

Also, note that we should provide a one-page worked example that includes: baseline tokens, burst snapshot, float pool draw, applied credits, invoiceable overage, and net invoice delta. I can draft that table if Olga wants to keep the workbook for internal reference.

Lina —

Great questions — please see the attached worked example and the updated pricing CSV. Short answers first: 

- Float pool funding/return: default is refundable at contract end as an invoice credit or cash refund (customer option indicated at signature). Refund timeline: standard 30–60 days post-contract termination after reconciliation.
- Worked example: attached XLSX shows baseline 1.2B tokens/month, a month with 4x burst (4.8B tokens), float pool funded at 15% of average monthly baseline (180M tokens), drawdown logic, and a quarterly true-up that posts as credit lines on the invoice. See the "Quarterly True-Up" tab for the journal entries.
- Dedicated capacity thresholds: Dedicated tier pricing kicks in at commit >= 10B tokens/month. Below that, Hosted API tiers apply (we included both rows).
- SLA/Remedy: We propose standard latency SLOs in the SOW with financial credits capped at 2% of monthly invoice for sustained breach; we can escalate that to a higher cap under enterprise negotiation.

Attachments: pricing_worked_example.xlsx (xlsx), pricing_sheet_v2.csv (csv)

Summary example (abridged):
- Baseline month charge: 1.2B tokens * $0.0006 = $720,000
- Burst month: 4.8B tokens. Float pool absorbs 180M tokens -> remaining overage = 3.48B tokens
- Overage pricing (tiered): first 1B @ $0.0009, next 2.48B @ $0.0007 -> net incremental overage = $ (compute in sheet)
- Quarterly true-up: under-utilization credit applied as negative invoice line; float pool replenishment spread over next 2 months

If you prefer, we will export the key rows into a CSV compatible with your procurement system and post the DocuSign envelope for signature of the commercial term sheet.

Next steps I propose:
- Lina: confirm refund preference for the float pool (cash vs credit).
- Karthik / Marissa: finalize the overage cap wording and SLA credit cap for the term sheet.
